# Executive leadership and governance

<!-- Generated by scripts/package/render_roles.py. Edit the YAML source, not this file. -->

**Department id:** `executive`  
**Mission:** Set direction, allocate resources, decide trade-offs between functions and stay accountable to owners and the law.

## Startup stage

In a 2–5 person company the founders hold all of these. The CEO role is whoever owns the decision log; CTO/CPO are usually one technical founder; CFO, CMO, CISO, CHRO and CLO are part-time hats plus outside professionals (accountant, counsel). Do not create separate agents for roles the stage does not need.

## Agents operating in this department

`corporate-orchestrator`, `ceo-strategy`, `coo-operations`, `cto-technology`, `cpo-product`, `cfo-finance`, `cmo-marketing`, `ciso-security`, `clo-legal`

## Roles

### Board and governance

Role id: `board-governance`

| Field | Definition |
|---|---|
| Mission | Oversee strategy, risk, finances and executive performance on behalf of owners. |
| Scope of responsibility | Approve strategy, budgets, major contracts, fundraising, executive hiring; ensure legal compliance. |
| Core activities | Quarterly review of strategy and metrics; Risk and audit oversight; Approval of major commitments |
| Inputs | Executive reports; Financial statements; Risk register |
| Outputs and deliverables | Approved strategy and budget; Governance decisions; Minutes |
| Decisions it can make | Fundraising; Executive appointments; Major contracts |
| Decisions requiring approval | Statutory obligations defined by jurisdiction |
| Collaborating roles | ceo; cfo; legal |
| Reporting relationship | Owners / shareholders |
| KPIs | Plan vs actual; Runway; Compliance incidents |
| Quality expectations | Decisions recorded with rationale and dissent |
| Tools and resources | Board pack template; Decision log |
| Common failure modes | Rubber-stamping; Reviewing vanity metrics; Ignoring risk register |
| Appropriate AI autonomy | advise |
| Human approval requirements | All decisions are human |

### Chief Executive Officer

Role id: `ceo`

| Field | Definition |
|---|---|
| Mission | Own the company's objective, strategy and the final call when functions disagree. |
| Scope of responsibility | Strategy, culture, fundraising, key relationships, executive team, go/no-go decisions. |
| Core activities | Decide segment and wedge; Arbitrate trade-offs; Communicate with investors and customers; Own the decision log |
| Inputs | Opportunity assessment; Gate verdicts; Financial model; Risk register |
| Outputs and deliverables | Strategic decisions with rationale; Priorities; Approval records |
| Decisions it can make | Direction; Priorities; Go/no-go at opportunity; product and release gates |
| Decisions requiring approval | Board-level items; spend above delegated limits |
| Collaborating roles | All department leads |
| Reporting relationship | Board |
| KPIs | Validated-learning cadence; Revenue and retention; Runway; Team health |
| Quality expectations | Decisions cite evidence and state what would change them |
| Tools and resources | Memory ledger; Decision log; Gate verdicts |
| Common failure modes | Deciding on narrative instead of evidence; Overriding safety or legal findings; Changing the objective silently |
| Appropriate AI autonomy | advise |
| Human approval requirements | Every executive decision is confirmed by the human owner |

### Chief Information Security Officer

Role id: `ciso`

|---|---|
| Mission | Keep security and privacy risk visible, authorised and owned. |

| Inputs | Threat models; Findings; Scan results; Privacy analyses |
| Outputs and deliverables | Risk acceptances; Testing authorisations; Incident policy |

| Decisions requiring approval | Critical findings cannot be accepted; regulated-data decisions with legal |
| Collaborating roles | cybersecurity; engineering; infrastructure; legal |
| Reporting relationship | CEO |
| KPIs | Open high/critical findings and age; Time to remediate; Incidents |
